intent: Arrows at both ends of a row or column that is too long to fit, so people can move it along without a scrollbar.
useWhen: A row of Scorecards, chips, or cards that runs past the edge
A row of Badge chips that runs past the edge
A tall list in a narrow column, scrolled up and down
doNotUseWhen: Paged slides or a gallery with Slide N of M — use Carousel
A second scrolling box inside the run — turn that one's scrolling off

children.note: The run that scrolls (Scoreboard, a row of Badge chips, a stack of cards). Not an items[] of slides.

orientation.note: Horizontal: arrows left/right. Vertical: arrows above/below; the Conveyor needs a height.

step.note: Pixels one press moves. Omit: 80% of the visible size.

label.note: Names the group and the arrows (“Scroll key metrics right”). Scoreboard passes its aria-label.

requirements: The run is a group with the label, and a focus stop, so the arrow keys scroll it
Each arrow is a kit Button that says what it does, like Scroll key metrics right
An arrow turns off at its end of the run
Smooth scrolling is off when the person prefers reduced motion
Narrower than --grid-breakpoint-sm (40rem): arrows give way to swipe; keys still move it

doNot: Do not use Conveyor for paged slides or a gallery — use Carousel
Do not use Conveyor to page a table — use Pagination
Do not put a second scrolling box inside it; pass scroll={false} on Scoreboard
Do not invent ScrollArea, Overflow, Marquee, or a local scroller
Do not use embla or Carousel internals
Do not add loop, showIndex, or slidesPerView
Do not use variant=primary on the arrows — tertiary icon-only only
snippet:
<Conveyor label="Key metrics">
  <Scoreboard scroll={false} items={[{ label: 'Revenue', value: '$48.2k' }, { label: 'Churn', value: '1.2%' }, { label: 'Users', value: '12.4k' }, { label: 'NPS', value: '64' }, { label: 'Tickets', value: '38' }]} />
</Conveyor>
